claim: For a finite Gibbs CE observable family, real coefficients, two independent continuous complex Fréchet derivations, a self-adjoint Gibbs Hamiltonian with positive real partition, and self-adjointness of the first weighted aggregate CE readout, the weighted pairwise centered-BKM bilinear response equals both the dissipative bilinear form of the finite Gibbs CE Onsager system at the weighted aggregate observable and the real mixed Gibbs log-partition Hessian of the two aggregate readouts.

carrier.type: Finite family Fin m → GibbsOperator n with actual finiteCEOperatorForm : Op1Form ℝ (realDerivationsLane (GibbsOperator n)).L (GibbsOperator n), constructed from the existing component extraction of an NOperatorForm CE family; quotient response carrier GibbsOperator n ⧸ scalarGauge n
operations: real coefficient-weighted finite family sums in the observable and readout carriers
the quotientBKMForm real bilinear form and its centeredBKMRealCovariance readout
the finite Gibbs CE Onsager system dissipative bilinear form
the real second Fréchet variation of the additive finite Gibbs log-partition
conventions: the two derivations D and E are independent and induce directions in the same real derivation lane
the (i,j) pairwise term is Cov_BKM(finiteCEOperatorForm(a_i,D), finiteCEOperatorForm(a_j,E)) weighted by c_i c_j
the aggregate observable is the actual operator ∑ i, c i • a i, and its readout is identified by finiteGibbsCEFamily_weightedReadout_eq
self-adjointness is required on the first aggregate readout, matching the existing Gibbs Hessian theorem
no nonnegativity is asserted for a mixed response; the diagonal positivity theorem is separate

smallest_gap.description: First prove the bilinear finite-family expansion for two independent derivation directions using the existing scalar-gauge quotient BKM form. Then use the proved finite weighted-readout identity and the existing finite Gibbs CE Onsager/Hessian identity. Keep the Hessian's self-adjointness hypothesis on the first actual aggregate readout only; do not assert nonnegativity for mixed directions or identify individual pairwise entries as Hessians without their own first-readout hypotheses.

out_of_scope: Nonnegativity of the mixed D,E response when D and E are distinct

Time-reversal parity reciprocity or nonvanishing curvature response
Infinite-dimensional Gibbs/Onsager or universal colimit results
